tob-10057: Missionary scholar Samuel Zwemer writes a sympathetic life of Al-Ghazali, the eleventh-century Muslim thinker he calls a ‘seeker after God.’ The book presents Ghazali’s spiritual quest as the finest expression of Islamic devotion, aimed at Christian readers curious about Islam at its most earnest. tob-10957: Proclus was the last great philosopher of pagan antiquity, and this work is his systematic theology of the Platonic gods. tob-4057: The fourth volume rounds out Blavatsky’s Secret Doctrine with more hidden teaching on the secret past of faiths and the veiled powers of nature. tob-4157: Andrew Lang’s daring book held that belief in a high god came first in man’s story — not last, as the wise men of his day taught. tob-0157: This Sacred Books of the East volume strings the English Zend Avesta — Vendidad, Yashts, and fellow Zoroastrian books. Turned by Darmesteter, Mills, and others, it bore Persia’s old faith to English readers. The book is needful for students of matched faiths.
tob-10257: The Rosarium Philosophorum — the Rosary of the Philosophers — is the great illustrated alchemical collection of the late Middle Ages. tob-10457: Molinos’s Spiritual Torrents is the classic of Quietism — the Spanish priest’s guide to the prayer of stillness. He taught total abandonment to God and the death of self-will. Condemned in 1687, his teaching lived on underground. The book remains a landmark of contemplative literature.
the-diary-and-letters-of-madame-d-arblay: Fanny Burney — Madame D'Arblay — kept one of the great diaries in English, and this volume covers her years at the court of George III. arxiv-2605-08857: Conformal prediction wraps a model's guesses in honest uncertainty bands, but it gets expensive on big data.
